svg.aria-label: Shot size by bird, pellets drawn at relative size. Steel number 4 for teal and very close shots. Steel 3 for medium ducks and decoying birds. Steel 2 for all round ducks. Steel BB for geese. Upland: number 7.5 for quail, number 6 for grouse. Bigger number means smaller pellet.
svg.text: Bigger number = smaller pellet. Drawn to scale.

g.data-tip: Non toxic only|Ducks, geese, coots and snipe: steel, bismuth, tungsten or tin. No lead in your pockets or boat.
Steel 4|Teal and very close shots. Teal over decoys: steel 4 to 6.
Steel 3|Medium ducks and close decoying birds.
Steel 2: the all round load|The all round duck load. Steel is lighter than lead, so go two sizes bigger than the old lead advice. Max range for you: 35 m (38 yd) (Tip).
Steel BB|The all round pellet for large Canada geese. BBB and T for longer shots. Aim at the head, not the whole bird (Tip).
Lead is legal for upland|Lead is legal for BC upland birds: grouse, ptarmigan, quail, partridge, pheasants and turkey. Hunting ducks the same day? Carry only steel (Tip).
Quail: #7.5|1 to 1 1/8 ounce loads. A .22 is not legal for quail: use the shotgun.
Grouse: #6|1 to 1 1/8 ounce loads. A .22 is legal for grouse too: head shots only (Tip).
